answer.rationale: p99 latency spike confined to primary region correlates temporally with release 2 hours ago. memory_b1 demonstrates rollback as effective mitigation for release-induced errors with minimal customer impact. memory_b6 shows staged gating catches regressions early. Verification of memory_b1 confirms rollback safety profile. Regional failover (memory_b2) is viable but rollback addresses root cause directly and preserves write locality during settlement peak. Capacity addition (memory_b3) would take longer and doesn't address release regression. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) prevent cascade but don't fix primary latency. Read replicas (memory_b5) only help dashboard load, not write path. Given settlement traffic at peak, rollback minimizes risk to write availability and allows fast recovery if regression is release-caused. Small guarded test scope preserves rollback as fallback if needed.
